children: Australia's current account deficit widened in the June quarter as imports of fuel and vehicles climbed, data showed on Tuesday, while net exports added modestly to economic growth.

Data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics out on Tuesday showed the current account ran a deficit of A$27.2 billion  ($19.50 billion) in the June quarter, from a revised A$25.4 billion the previous quarter. That compared with forecasts for a A$30 billion shortfall.
The ABS said net exports would add 0.1 percentage point to gross domestic product in the second quarter, compared with analyst forecasts of a neutral impact.
